details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its key interest rates by 25 basis points on Thursday, September 10, 2026, marking the second hike this year. This decision pushes the deposit rate to 2.5% as the central bank aims to combat energy-driven inflation, which has been exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Iran. The ECB revised its 2026 economic growth projection upward to 0.9% but now expects inflation to average 3.0% this year and 2.5% in 2027, both above its 2% target. Financial markets are anticipating further rate increases, although the ECB has not explicitly pre-committed to future policy moves.
title: ECB Hikes Rates Second Time in 2026 Amid Iran War Inflation Fears

details: The U.S. economy added a robust 162,000 jobs in August 2026, significantly surpassing economists' forecasts, with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.1%. This unexpectedly strong labor market data, coupled with upward revisions to job gains in previous months, has intensified market expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at its upcoming September meeting. Following the report's release, Bitcoin experienced a dip, while U.S. Treasury yields climbed, and the dollar strengthened, reflecting investor concerns about a more hawkish monetary policy stance.
title: Strong US August Jobs Report Bolsters Fed Rate Hike Expectations

details: Government bond yields across major developed economies, including the U.S., Japan, and Germany, have reached multi-decade highs. This global bond market sell-off is primarily driven by persistent inflation concerns, substantial government and corporate borrowing (partly fueled by investments in artificial intelligence), and the growing expectation that central banks will maintain restrictive monetary policies for a longer period than previously anticipated. The rising yields signify tightening financial conditions worldwide, increasing borrowing costs for governments and businesses.
title: Global Bond Yields Surge Amid Inflation and Central Bank Hawkishness
